

```{r, include=FALSE}
# Import Libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(dplyr)

library(stringr)

library(caret)
library(e1071)

```


### 1. Data Preparation
#### 1.1. Data Filtering
```{r}
# Filter Tourists with "Holiday / Vacation" as Primary or Secondary Travel Purpose
survey_main_header <- read.csv(
  "./dataset for modeling/survey_main_header.csv",
  header = TRUE
)

secondary_purpose_of_visit <- read.csv(
  "./dataset for modeling/secondary_purpose_of_visit.csv",
  header = TRUE
)

combined_df <- inner_join(
  survey_main_header,
  secondary_purpose_of_visit,
  by = "response_id"
)

duplicate_rows <- combined_df |>
  count(response_id) |>
  filter(n > 1) |>
  select(response_id)

filtered_combined_df <- combined_df |>
  filter(!response_id %in% duplicate_rows$response_id)

purpose <- filtered_combined_df |>
  select(
    response_id,
    purpose_of_visit_main,
    purpose_subtype,
    reasons_for_travel_secondary
  )

purpose |>
  group_by(purpose_of_visit_main) |>
  summarise(n = n())

purpose |>
  group_by(reasons_for_travel_secondary) |>
  summarise(n = n()) 

tourist_response_ids <- purpose |>
  filter(
    reasons_for_travel_secondary == "Holiday / vacation" |
      purpose_of_visit_main == "Holiday / vacation"
  ) |>
  pull(response_id)

tourist_survey_main_header <- survey_main_header |>
  filter(response_id %in% tourist_response_ids)
```


#### 1.2. Merge Tables
```{r}
# Filter tourist records in other tables based on selected response_ids, and merge into a consolidated table

# Select relevant columns from tourist_survey_main_header for modeling
tourist_survey_main_header <- tourist_survey_main_header |>
  select(response_id, age_range, country_of_residence, gender, no_days_in_nz)

# Load additional tables containing satisfaction and expenditure information
visitor_satisfaction <- read.csv(
  "./dataset for modeling/visitor_satisfaction.csv",
  header = TRUE
)

expenditure_by_industry <- read.csv(
  "./dataset for modeling/expenditure_by_industry.csv",
  header = TRUE
)

# Filter satisfaction and expenditure records corresponding to the selected tourist response_ids
tourist_visitor_satisfaction <- visitor_satisfaction |>
  filter(response_id %in% tourist_response_ids)

tourist_expenditure <- expenditure_by_industry |>
  filter(response_id %in% tourist_response_ids)

# Merge all datasets on response_id to create a unified tourist dataset
tourist_full <- tourist_survey_main_header |>
  left_join(tourist_visitor_satisfaction, by = "response_id") |>
  left_join(tourist_expenditure, by = "response_id")

```


#### 1.3 Data Transformation and Data Cleaning
```{r}
# 1. Select features relevant for modeling
tourist_full <- tourist_full |>
  select(response_id, age_range, country_of_residence, gender, no_days_in_nz,
         satisfaction_rating, cost_accomm, cost_dom_travel, cost_food_drink,
         cost_entertainment, cost_shopping, cost_other, cost_tour_package,
         cost_dom_flights, cost_car_rentals, cost_eating_out,
         cost_day_cruise, exc_cost_int_flights, exc_cost_multi_night_cruise,
         exc_cost_travel_insurance)

# 2. Encode categorical variables as factors
tourist_full <- tourist_full |>
  mutate(
    age_range = as.factor(age_range),
    gender = as.factor(gender),
    country_of_residence = as.factor(country_of_residence)
  )

# 3. Create the 'total_spending' feature by summing all relevant cost components
tourist_full <- tourist_full |>
  mutate(
    total_spending = rowSums(
      across(
        c(cost_accomm, cost_dom_travel, cost_food_drink,
          cost_entertainment, cost_shopping, cost_other,
          cost_tour_package, cost_dom_flights, cost_car_rentals,
          cost_eating_out, cost_day_cruise, exc_cost_int_flights,
          exc_cost_multi_night_cruise, exc_cost_travel_insurance),
        ~ replace_na(., 0)  # Replace missing cost values with zero before summing
      )
    )
  )

# 4. Remove records with missing values in essential fields
tourist_full <- tourist_full |>
  filter(
    !is.na(age_range),
    !is.na(country_of_residence),
    !is.na(gender),
    !is.na(no_days_in_nz),
    !is.na(total_spending),
    !is.na(satisfaction_rating)
  )

# 5. Transform 'satisfaction_rating' from text to numeric and derive a binary satisfaction label
tourist_full <- tourist_full |>
  mutate(
    satisfaction_rating = str_extract(satisfaction_rating, "^[0-9]") |> as.numeric(),
    satisfaction_binary = ifelse(satisfaction_rating %in% c(1, 2), "Low", "High"),
    satisfaction_binary = as.factor(satisfaction_binary)
  )

# 6. Finalize the dataset with selected features for modeling
model_data <- tourist_full |>
  select(
    response_id,
    age_range,
    country_of_residence,
    gender,
    no_days_in_nz,
    total_spending,
    satisfaction_binary
  )
```



### 2. Modeling - Naive Bayes
```{r}
# 2.1. Stratified split into training and testing sets (80% training, 20% testing)
set.seed(123)
train_index <- createDataPartition(tourist_full$satisfaction_binary, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)

train_data <- tourist_full[train_index, ]
test_data <- tourist_full[-train_index, ]

# 2.2. Oversample the "Low" class in the training set only
# Extract "Low" samples
low_samples <- train_data |>
  filter(satisfaction_binary == "Low")

# Oversample "Low" samples to balance with "High" samples
low_samples_oversampled <- low_samples |>
  sample_frac(size = (sum(train_data$satisfaction_binary == "High") / sum(train_data$satisfaction_binary == "Low")), replace = TRUE)

# Combine the original training set with the oversampled "Low" samples
train_data_balanced <- bind_rows(
  train_data,
  low_samples_oversampled
)

# Check the new class distribution in the balanced training set
table(train_data_balanced$satisfaction_binary)


# 2.3. Train the Naive Bayes model (with Laplace smoothing to avoid zero probabilities)
nb_model <- naiveBayes(
  satisfaction_binary ~ age_range + country_of_residence + gender + no_days_in_nz + total_spending,
  data = train_data_balanced,
  laplace = 1
)

# 2.4. Make predictions on the testing set
nb_predictions <- predict(nb_model, newdata = test_data)

# 2.5. Evaluate the model performance using a confusion matrix
confusionMatrix(nb_predictions, test_data$satisfaction_binary)


```
